set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule for the County land program itself. A ground lease or sale below fair market value is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(3), and whether a project is covered depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The County Measure A gap loans paired with these sites carry the County of Santa Clara Prevailing Wage Requirements for County-funded projects (as restated in the Housing Trust Silicon Valley Supportive Housing Fund Guidelines Section 7.1, https://housingtrustsv.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/Supportive-Housing-Fund-Guidelines.pdf), but no County document read states that rule for the land conveyances.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; depends on 1720(b)(3) land terms, 1720(c) exemptions and whether County loans are in the deal. Confirm with OSH and the site disposition agreement.

reason: The Board legislative file 129854 and its two attachments do not address prevailing wage, and no County rule specific to land conveyances was found, so the trigger stays unclear.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: The MHIP staff memo does not address prevailing wage. Construction tax and in-lieu fee reductions are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (fees reduced or waived by a political subdivision), but coverage depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts; no DIR determination or City rule on MHIP was found.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; only basis is Labor Code 1720(b)(4) fee waivers, outcome depends on 1720(c) and project facts.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR public works coverage determinations PW 2006-001 (Horizons at Indio, March 12, 2007, citing PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe, publicly offered conduit bonds) and PW 2006-006 (Tracy Place Senior Apartments, July 11, 2006, privately placed CDLAC bonds bought by a bank) hold that conduit multifamily bond financing is not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) because proceeds and repayments never enter public coffers, and that LIHTCs are not public funds. San Jose acts as conduit issuer under Council Policy 1-16, and the April 28, 2026 Policy amendment memo imposes no prevailing wage requirement. Other public subsidy layered on the project (City or County loans, land, fee waivers) is analyzed separately and can still trigger prevailing wage. Sources: https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf ; https://www.Dir.Ca.Gov/OPRL/coverage/year2006/2006-006.pdf

reason: DIR determinations PW 2006-001 and PW 2006-006 hold that conduit multifamily bond financing, public or private placement, is not public funds under Labor Code 1720.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: Supportive Housing Fund Guidelines Section 5.1 and Section 7.1 (County of Santa Clara Prevailing Wage Requirements): borrowers must comply, and except for projects of $1,000 or less, vendors performing building construction, alteration, demolition or repair must pay all workers on County-funded projects prevailing wage under Labor Code sections 1770 through 1777.7. Source: https://housingtrustsv.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/Supportive-Housing-Fund-Guidelines.pdf (guidelines date from 2017; confirm current terms with the Housing Trust).

reason: The program guidelines Sections 5.1 and 7.1 require County of Santa Clara prevailing wage on funded construction work over $1,000.
